entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Patna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Date: 16-07-2015  Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned APP for  the State.

2. The present petition has been filed for quashing the order  dated 25.02.2010 passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate,
 Aurangabad in connection with G.O. Case No. 14 of 2010 for the offences  under Sections 16(1) (a) (i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the analysis  report dated 07.12.2009 issued by the Combined Food & Drug Laboratory,
 Agam Kuan, Patna as contained in Annexure-5 of the petition, merely  discloses the presence of water soluble colours and it is opined that the  sample of Masur Dal does not conform to the prescribed standard of purity Rama Shankar Prasad vs State Of Bihar & Anr on 16 July, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135755907/
1  laid down under the P.F.A. Rules and hence adulterated.

sentences.text: It is howev  submitted that there is nothing in the said report to suggest that such the  Patna High Court Cr.Misc. No.14356 of 2013 dt.16-07-2015   water soluble colour was of a nature injurious to health or otherwise  for human consumption and as such the petitioner ought not to be  prosecuted.

4. This Court has considered this aspect of the matter in a nu  decisions including Cr. Misc. No. 16358 of 2010 disposed of on 06.01.
 (Awadh Bihari Lal vs. The State of Bihar), Cr. Misc. No. 16282 of 201  disposed of on 03.08.2012 (Binod Kumar Agrawal vs. The State of Bihar  Cr. Misc. No.48446 of 2012 disposed of on 14.05.2015 ( Sitaram Khaita  anr. vs. The State of Bihar) including 2010 (3) PLJR 120 (Rajeev Kuma  State of Bihar).

entities.text: Awadh Bihari Lal vs. The State of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sitaram Khaita  anr. vs. The State of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This Court has consistently taken the view that mere  presence of some colouring matter which was not found to be injurious  health not unfit for human consumption cannot justify the prosecution  petitioner.
 5.

In the above circumstances, the impugned order dated  25.02.2010 passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Aurangabad taking cognizance in connection with G.O. Case No. 14 of 2010 is hereby quashed.
